translations.literal: Hence in mountains and forests no brightness hides; at a hemp gate none linger idle.
translations.idiomatic: So hills hide no recluse worth hiring and cottage gates shelter no loiterer.

sentences.zh: 至承統之王，或是中才，或復凡人，居聖人之器，處兆庶之上，是以其教日穨，風俗漸弊。

translations.literal: When it comes to heirs who inherit the line—some are middling talent, some again common men—dwelling in the sage's vessel, placed above the myriad million—thereby their instruction daily declines and customs gradually spoil.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs who inherit power may be middling or merely ordinary yet wield the sage's authority over millions—teaching frays and customs rot.

sentences.zh: 又中才之君，所資者偏，物以類感，必於其黨，黨言雖非，彼以為是。

translations.literal: Moreover middling-talent lords rely on biased advisers—things move by kindred sympathy and surely toward their faction—faction speech though wrong, they take as right.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre rulers lean on partial counselors—like calls to like inside their clique—wrong counsel sounds right to them.

sentences.zh: 以所授有顏、冉之賢，所用有廊廟之器，居官者日冀元凱之功，在上者日庶堯、舜之義，彼豈知其政漸毀哉！

translations.literal: Suppose those appointed had the worth of Yan and Ran and those employed had hall-and-temple vessels—officeholders daily hoped for Yuan and Kai's merit; those above daily hoped for Yao and Shun's righteousness—how could they know their government gradually ruined!
translations.idiomatic: Give them ministers like Yan Hui and Ran Geng and tools fit for the ancestral hall—officials dream of Eight Yuan merit and rulers dream of Yao and Shun—yet they never see policy rotting beneath them!

sentences.zh: 朝雖有求賢之名，而無知才之實。

translations.literal: Though court had the name of seeking worthies, there was no reality of recognizing talent.
translations.idiomatic: Court keeps the slogan of seeking talent without the substance of judging it.

sentences.zh: 言雖當，彼以為誣；

translations.literal: Speech though right, they took as slander;
translations.idiomatic: Truth they call slander;

sentences.zh: 策雖奇，彼以為妄。

translations.literal: policy though marvelous, they took as wild.
translations.idiomatic: sound policy they dismiss as fantasy.

sentences.zh: 誣則毀己之言入，妄則不忠之責生，豈故為哉？

translations.literal: When it is slander, words that ruin oneself enter; when wild, charge of disloyalty arises—is it purposely so?
translations.idiomatic: Label counsel slander and self-serving flattery floods in; call it mad and charges of disloyalty follow—not by accident.

sentences.zh: 淺明不見深理，近才不睹遠體也。

translations.literal: Shallow clarity does not see deep principle; near talent does not behold distant scope.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow judgment cannot grasp depth; petty talent cannot see the whole.

sentences.zh: 是以言不用，計不施，恐死亡之不暇，何論功名之立哉！

translations.literal: Hence counsel is not used, plans not deployed—fearing they have no leisure for death—what talk of establishing merit and fame!
translations.idiomatic: Plans shelved and counsel ignored—men barely survive—what hope of fame?

sentences.zh: 故上官昵而屈原放，宰嚭寵而伍員戮，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Hence Shangguan was intimate and Qu Yuan was banished; Zai Pi was favored and Wu Yuan was executed—is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Jin won favor and Qu Yuan went into exile; Bo Pi rose and Wu Zixu died—what sorrow!

sentences.zh: 若仲舒抑于孝武，賈誼失于漢文，蓋復是其輕者耳。

translations.literal: As for Dong Zhongshu suppressed under Xiaowu, Jia Yi missing fit under Han Wen—those are still the lighter cases.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu slighted under Emperor Wu and Jia Yi stalled under Emperor Wen—among failures those rank as mild.

sentences.zh: 故白起有云：『非得賢之難，用之難。

translations.literal: Hence Bai Qi had a saying: 'It is not hard to obtain worthies—it is hard to employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Qi said, "Finding talent is easy—using it is hard.

sentences.zh: 非用之難，信之難。

translations.literal: It is not hard to employ them—it is hard to trust them.
translations.idiomatic: Using talent is easy—trusting it is hard."

sentences.zh: 』得賢而不能用，用而不能信，功業豈可得而成哉！」

translations.literal: ' Obtain worthies yet cannot employ them; employ yet cannot trust them—how can merit and enterprise be accomplished!'"
translations.idiomatic: Talent unused or trusted too late never builds an empire."

sentences.zh: 譚至洛陽，武帝親策之曰：「今四海一統，萬里同風，天下有道，莫斯之盛。

translations.literal: When Tan arrived at Luoyang, Emperor Wu personally examined him, saying: "Now the four seas are unified, ten thousand li share one wind; all under Heaven has the Way—none surpasses this flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan reached Luoyang, Emperor Wu examined him in person: "The realm is one; customs align for ten thousand li—never has the Way shone brighter.

sentences.zh: 然北有未羈之虜，西有醜施之氐，故謀夫未得高枕，邊人未獲晏然，將何以長弭斯患，混清六合？

translations.literal: Yet north there are unsubdued captives; west there are Choushi Di—hence strategists cannot pillow high and frontier folk do not obtain tranquillity—how shall We long quell these troubles and clarify and purify the six directions?
translations.idiomatic: Yet northern tribes remain outside the halter and western Di bands still stir—counselors cannot sleep easy nor border folk rest—how may we end these troubles and clear the whole realm?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣聞聖人之臨天下也，祖乾綱以流化，順穀風以興仁，兼三才以禦物，開四聰以招賢。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I have heard that when sages face all under Heaven, they take Heaven's guiding net as ancestor to spread transformation, comply with grain wind to raise benevolence, combine the three powers to manage things, open the four counsels to summon worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Sages who rule the realm anchor transformation in Heaven's pattern, ride the east wind of spring to nurture kindness, wield heaven-earth-man together, and open every avenue of counsel to draw worthies."

sentences.zh: 故勞謙日昃，務在擇才，宣明岩穴，垂光隱滯。

translations.literal: Hence laboring in humility till sunset, the task lies in choosing talent, proclaiming brightness from cliff caves, shedding light on hidden obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: They toil humbly past noon—talent is everything—shine light into caves and lift men stalled in shadow.

sentences.zh: 俊乂龍躍，帝道以光；

translations.literal: Outstanding talents leap like dragons—the emperor's way thereby shines;
translations.idiomatic: Heroes rise like dragons—the royal path gleams;

sentences.zh: 清德風翔，王化克舉。

translations.literal: pure virtue wind-soars—kingly transformation is able to rise.
translations.idiomatic: pure virtue rides the wind—kingly transformation takes hold.

sentences.zh: 是以皋陶見舉，不仁者遠；

translations.literal: Hence when Gaoyao was promoted, the unkindly stood far off;
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyao once lifted—the cruel fled;

sentences.zh: 陸賈重漢，遠夷折節。

translations.literal: Lu Jia esteemed Han—distant barbarians bent the knee.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jia lent Han weight—distant tribes bowed.

sentences.zh: 今聖朝德音發於帷幄，清風翔乎無外，戎旗南指，江、漢席捲；

translations.literal: Now the sacred court's virtuous sound issues from the curtain and canopy; pure wind soars without exterior limit—martial banners point south—the Yangzi and Han are swept like mat rolls;
translations.idiomatic: Today virtuous edicts leave Your tent and wholesome wind blows boundless—banners wheel south and the Yangzi and Han roll up like mats;

sentences.zh: 干戈西征，羌蠻慕化，誠闡四門之秋，興禮教之日也。

translations.literal: spears west campaign—Qiang and Man admire transformation—it is truly the season for opening the four gates and the day for raising ritual instruction.
translations.idiomatic: arms march west while Qiang and Man yearn for civilization—the hour to open every gate and lift ritual teaching.

sentences.zh: 故髦俊聞聲而響赴，殊才望險而雲集。

translations.literal: Hence splendid talents hearing the sound echo and hasten; unusual talents sighting peril cloud-gather.
translations.idiomatic: Fine men race toward Your summons; odd talents flock despite hardship.

sentences.zh: 虛高館以俟賢，設重爵以待士，急善過於饑渴，用人疾于影響，杜佞諂之門，廢鄭聲之樂，混清六合，實由乎此。

translations.literal: Empty lofty lodges to await worthies; set weighty noble ranks to await scholars; urgency toward good surpasses hunger and thirst; employing men quick as shadow and echo—block flattery's gates; abolish Zheng music—clarifying and purifying the six directions truly proceeds from this.
translations.idiomatic: Leave great halls open for talent, stack noble titles for scholars, thirst for goodness more than food or drink, appoint men swift as echo—shut flattery's door and silence licentious music—purifying the realm begins here.

sentences.zh: 雖西北有未羈之寇，殊漠有不朝之虜，征之則勞師，得之則無益，故班固云：'有其地不可耕而食，得其人不可臣而畜，來則懲而禦之，去則備而守之。

translations.literal: Though northwest have unsubdued raiders and distant desert have captives who do not court—punishing them wearies troops; obtaining them brings no benefit—hence Ban Gu said: 'Having their land, one cannot plow and eat; having their people, one cannot subject and herd them—when they come, chastise and withstand them; when they depart, prepare and guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest raiders and desert tribes who skip court cost dear to chase and yield little gain—Ban Gu warned: their soil will not feed us, their men will not obey—strike when they come, guard when they flee.

sentences.zh: '蓋安邊之術也。」

translations.literal: ' This covers the art of pacifying frontiers.'"
translations.idiomatic: That is how borders stay quiet."

sentences.zh: 又策曰：「吳、蜀恃險，今既蕩平。

translations.literal: Again the examination said: "Wu and Shu relied on peril—now they have been swept flat.
translations.idiomatic: The examination continued: "Wu and Shu trusted their barriers—both are crushed.

sentences.zh: 蜀人服化，無攜貳之心；

translations.literal: Shu people submit to transformation—without hearts of divided allegiance;
translations.idiomatic: Shu accepts civilization—no hint of split loyalty;

sentences.zh: 而吳人趑雎，屢作妖寇。

translations.literal: but Wu people hesitate and rear—repeatedly acting demonic bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Wu vacillates and stirs trouble again and again.

sentences.zh: 豈蜀人敦朴，易可化誘；

translations.literal: Is it that Shu people are honest and plain—easy to transform and entice;
translations.idiomatic: Are Shu folk simpler—easier to win;

sentences.zh: 吳人輕銳，難安易動乎？

translations.literal: Wu people light and keen—hard to pacify and easy to stir?
translations.idiomatic: Wu quicker and keener—harder to settle?

sentences.zh: 今將欲綏靜新附，何以為先？

translations.literal: Now desiring to pacify and quiet the newly attached—what comes first?
translations.idiomatic: How shall we calm the newly conquered—what comes first?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣聞漢末分崩，英雄鼎峙，蜀棲岷隴，吳據江表。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I have heard that at Han's end it split and collapsed—heroes tripod-stood—Shu perched on Min and Long—Wu held the lands beyond the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Late Han shattered—warlords tripod-balanced—Shu clung to Min and Long, Wu gripped the eastern rivers.

sentences.zh: 至大晉龍興，應期受命，文皇運籌，安樂順軌；

translations.literal: When great Jin dragon rose, answering the period and receiving the mandate—Literary Emperor laid plans—peace and joy followed the track;
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin rose on time—Emperor Wen mapped strategy—peace fell into line;

sentences.zh: 聖上潛謀，歸命向化。

translations.literal: the sacred sovereign secretly plotted—submitting mandate toward transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty shaped destiny in secret until foes bent to civilization.

sentences.zh: 蜀染化日久，風教遂成；

translations.literal: Shu long steeped in transformation—wind instruction thereupon completed;
translations.idiomatic: Shu soaked in influence until custom hardened;

sentences.zh: 吳始初附，未改其化，非為蜀人敦愨而吳人易動也。

translations.literal: Wu only lately attached—not yet changed in transformation—it is not that Shu people are honest and sincere while Wu people easy to stir.
translations.idiomatic: Wu submitted late—habits lag—not because Shu is steadier by nature.

sentences.zh: 然殊俗遠境，風土不同，吳阻長江，舊俗輕悍。

translations.literal: Yet alien customs and distant borders—wind and soil differ—Wu blocks the long Yangzi—old customs light and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier peoples differ—Wu hugs the great river—its temper stays quick and bold.

sentences.zh: 所安之計，當先籌其人士，使雲翔閶闔，進其賢才，待以異禮；

translations.literal: The plan for settling them ought first to arrange their gentlemen and scholars—making them cloud-soar at Chang'e Gate—advance their worthy talents—treat them with unusual ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Peace them by lifting local gentlemen—bring talent to court with honors;

sentences.zh: 明選牧伯，致以威風；

translations.literal: clearly select shepherds and elders—bring to them awe-inspiring wind;
translations.idiomatic: pick firm governors to lend dignity;

sentences.zh: 輕其賦斂，將順咸悅，可以永保無窮，長為人臣者也。」

translations.literal: lighten their levies—lead compliant—all pleased—can eternally preserve without limit—long be men's ministers.'"
translations.idiomatic: ease taxes and follow local feeling—they stay pleased subjects forever."

sentences.zh: 又策曰：「聖人稱如有王者，必世而後仁。

translations.literal: Again the examination said: "The sage pronounced—if there were a king—it must be a generation before benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The examination asked: "The sage said benevolent rule needs a generation to ripen.

sentences.zh: 今天成地平，大化無外，雖匈奴未羈，羌、氐驕黠，將修文德以綏之，舞干戚以來之，故兵戈載戢，武夫寢息。

translations.literal: Now Heaven completes and earth levels—great transformation without exterior—though Xiongnu not bridled, Qiang and Di arrogant and cunning—will cultivate pattern virtue to pacify them, dance shields and axes to draw them—hence weapons stored away—warriors sleep and rest.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth align—culture spreads beyond borders—though Xiongnu remain free and Qiang or Di grow bold, civil virtue will soothe them and the shield-dance summon them—arms rest and soldiers sleep.

sentences.zh: 如此，已可消鋒刃為佃器，罷尚方武庫之用未邪？

translations.literal: Thus—is it already possible to melt blades into farming tools and cease employment of the imperial workshops and martial arsenals?
translations.idiomatic: May we yet beat swords into ploughshares and idle the armories?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「夫唐堯曆載，頌聲乃作；

translations.literal: " He replied: "As for Tang Yao passing years—only then did praise sound arise;
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Even under Yao ages passed before songs of praise rose;

sentences.zh: 文、武相承，禮樂大同。

translations.literal: Wen and Wu succeeded each other—ritual and music greatly unified.
translations.idiomatic: Kings Wen and Wu handed power until ritual and music harmonized.

sentences.zh: 清一八紘，綏蕩無外，萬國順軌，海內斐然。

translations.literal: Purifying one and eight cords—pacifying vastness without exterior—myriad states follow the track—within the seas splendid.
translations.idiomatic: They unified the zones, soothed every frontier, aligned ten thousand states—the realm glowed.

sentences.zh: 雖復被髮之鄉，徒跣之國，皆習章甫而入朝，要衣裳以磬折。

translations.literal: Though again lands of disheveled hair, states of bare feet—all practiced black caps and entered court—girdled robes and folded like sounding stone.
translations.idiomatic: Even bare-headed barefoot realms donned court caps and bent in silk—everyone aped the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 夫大舜之德，猶有三苗之征；

translations.literal: As for great Shun's virtue—still there was the punishment expedition against San Miao;
translations.idiomatic: Great Shun still campaigned against San Miao;

sentences.zh: 以周之盛，獫狁為寇。

translations.literal: considering Zhou's flourishing—the Xianyun were bandits.
translations.idiomatic: at Zhou's height the Xianyun still raided.

sentences.zh: 雖有文德，又須武備。

translations.literal: Though there is pattern virtue, martial preparedness is also needed.
translations.idiomatic: Civil virtue still needs martial readiness.

sentences.zh: 備預不虞，古之善教；

translations.literal: Preparing against unforeseen events is good teaching of antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: Readiness for surprise is ancient wisdom;

sentences.zh: 安不忘危，聖人常誡。

translations.literal: in peace not forgetting danger—sages constantly warn.
translations.idiomatic: in peace remember peril—the sages say so still.

sentences.zh: 無為罷武庫之常職，鑠鋒刃為佃器。

translations.literal: It is not fitting to abolish the standing duty of martial arsenals or melt blades into farming tools.
translations.idiomatic: Do not idle the armories or beat every sword into a ploughshare yet.

sentences.zh: 自可倒戢干戈，苞以獸皮，將帥之士，使為諸侯，于散樂休風，未為不泰也。」

translations.literal: Of itself one may store spears inverted, wrap them in beast hide, make commanders and generals into feudal lords—amid dissolving music and restorative wind, it is not untranquil.'"
translations.idiomatic: Lay arms aside wrapped in hide, enfeoff your captains if you will—under loosened music and gentle airs that still counts as peace."

sentences.zh: 又策曰：「夫法令之設，所以隨時制也。

translations.literal: Again the examination said: "As for the establishment of laws and orders—it is to regulate according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: The examination continued: "Laws fit their age.

sentences.zh: 時險則峻法以取平，時泰則寬網以將化。

translations.literal: When times are perilous then harsh law to obtain peace; when times are tranquil then loose nets to lead transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Danger demands stern statutes; calm seasons favor lenient nets.

sentences.zh: 今天下太平，四方無事，百姓承德，將就無為而乂。

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven is peaceful—the four directions without affair—common people receive virtue—about to approach doing nothing and governing.
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm is still—folk receive virtue—and government nears wuwei ease.

sentences.zh: 至於律令，應有所損益不？

translations.literal: As for statutes and ordinances—ought there be reduction or augmentation?
translations.idiomatic: Should statutes shrink or grow?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣聞五帝殊禮，三王異教，故或禪讓以光政，或干戈以攻取。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I have heard the Five Emperors had different ritual—the Three Kings different teaching—hence some abdicated to brighten government, some used arms to attack and take.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Five Emperors differed in rite, Three Kings in teaching—some yielded thrones, others conquered."

sentences.zh: 至於興禮樂以和人，流清風以寧俗，其歸一也。

translations.literal: When it comes to raising ritual and music to harmonize men, flowing pure wind to quiet customs—their return is one.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ritual and music calm the people—pure custom ends the same.

sentences.zh: 今誠風教大同，四海無虞，人皆感化，去邪從正。

translations.literal: Now truly wind and teaching greatly unify—the four seas without anxiety—all transformed—leave evil and follow right.
translations.idiomatic: Culture now unifies; beyond the frontiers all is still—men turn from vice.

sentences.zh: 夫以堯、舜之盛，而猶設象刑；

translations.literal: Consider Yao and Shun's flourishing—and still they established symbolic punishments;
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao and Shun kept model punishments;

sentences.zh: 殷、周之隆，而甫侯制律。

translations.literal: Yin and Zhou's grandeur—and the Marquis of Fu regulated statutes.
translations.idiomatic: glorious Yin and Zhou still ordered the codes through the Marquis of Fu.

sentences.zh: 律令之存，何妨於政。

translations.literal: That statutes and ordinances exist—what harm to government?
translations.idiomatic: Keeping the code on the books harms nothing.

sentences.zh: 若乃大道四達，禮樂交通，凡人修行，黎庶勵節，刑罰懸而不用，律令存而無施，適足以隆太平之雅化，飛仁風乎無外矣。」

translations.literal: If the great way runs four ways open—ritual and music intercourse—all men cultivate conduct—black-haired folk urge integrity—punishments hang unused—statutes exist unapplied—just sufficient to exalt the elegant transformation of great peace—and send benevolent wind flying without exterior.'"
translations.idiomatic: When the Way runs free and ritual joins music, common conduct rises—laws may hang unused yet stand ready—enough to crown an age of peace and spread kindness beyond the borders."

sentences.zh: 又策曰：「昔帝舜以二八成功，文王以多士興周。

translations.literal: Again the examination said: "Of old Emperor Shun succeeded with the Eight Ministers; King Wen raised Zhou with many scholars.
translations.idiomatic: The examination asked: "Shun used eight ministers; Wen built Zhou with many talents."

sentences.zh: 夫制化在於得人，而賢才難得。

translations.literal: Transformation lies in obtaining men—yet worthy talent is hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Order rests on men—yet worthies are rare.

sentences.zh: 今大統始同，宜搜才實。

translations.literal: Now the great unification has just aligned—it is fitting to search out substantial talent.
translations.idiomatic: The empire has just united—seek real ability.

sentences.zh: 州郡有貢薦之舉，猶未獲出群卓越之倫。

translations.literal: Prefectures and commanderies have nomination for tribute—still they have not obtained those who surpass the crowd and tower.
translations.idiomatic: Regions recommend candidates—yet none leap ahead of the pack.

sentences.zh: 將時無其人？

translations.literal: Is it that the times lack such persons?
translations.idiomatic: Are the times empty of genius?

sentences.zh: 有而致之未得其理也？

translations.literal: Or they exist but summoning them has not obtained the right pattern?
translations.idiomatic: Or do we fail to fetch them rightly?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣聞興化立法，非賢無以光其道；

translations.literal: " He replied: "I have heard that raising transformation and establishing law—without worthies none can brighten its way;
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Law and transformation need worthies to shine."

sentences.zh: 平世理亂，非才無以宣其業。

translations.literal: ordering an age and settling chaos—without talent none can proclaim its enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Peace and peril alike need talent enacted."

sentences.zh: 上自皇羲，下及帝王，莫不張惶綱以羅遠，飛仁風以被物。

translations.literal: Above from august Xi down to emperors and kings—none failed to spread the guiding net to catch the distant, fly benevolent wind to cover things.
translations.idiomatic: From high antiquity every throne cast its net wide and sent kindness abroad.

sentences.zh: 故得賢則教興，失人則政廢。

translations.literal: Hence obtain worthies then teaching rises; lose men then government wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Find talent and instruction thrives—miss it and policy rots.

sentences.zh: 今四海一統，萬里同風，州郡貢秀孝，台府簡良才，以八紘之廣，兆庶之眾，豈當無卓越俊逸之才乎！

translations.literal: Now the four seas unified, ten thousand li one wind—prefectures tribute cultivated and filial—grand offices pick good talent—with the eight cords' breadth and the multitude's mass—how could there fail to be surpassing and superior persons!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is one—regions send nominees—the court selects—with so vast a population how could excellence be absent?

sentences.zh: 譬猶南海不少明月之寶，大宛不乏千里之駒也。

translations.literal: It is like the Southern Sea not lacking bright-moon pearls—Dayuan not lacking thousand-li foals.
translations.idiomatic: The south still hides luminous pearls; Ferghana still breeds swift horses.

sentences.zh: 異哲難見，遠數難睹，故堯、舜太平之化，二八由舜而甫顯，殷湯革王之命，伊尹負鼎而方用。

translations.literal: Different sages are hard to see—distant reckonings hard to behold—hence Yao and Shun's peaceful transformation—the Eight Ministers through Shun only then appeared—Tang of Yin altering the king's mandate—Yi Yin bore the tripod only then was employed.
translations.idiomatic: Rare genius hides far off—the Eight Ministers shone only after Shun; Yi Yin carried his cauldron before Tang used him.

sentences.zh: 當今聖朝禮亡國之士，接遐裔之人，或貂蟬於帷幄，或剖符於千里，巡狩必有呂公之遇，宵夢必有岩穴之感。

translations.literal: Now the sacred court treats scholars of fallen states, receives men from distant shores—some with marten tails in the curtain—some splitting tallies across a thousand li—tour inspections surely meet a Duke Lü—midnight dreams surely touch cliff caves.
translations.idiomatic: Today You honor fallen dynasties' men—some advise within the tent, some govern regions—like kings who meet worthies on tour or in dream.

sentences.zh: 賢俊之出，可企踵而待也。」

translations.literal: The emergence of worthy excellence—can stand on tiptoe and await.'"
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men will appear—wait on tiptoe."

sentences.zh: 時九州秀孝策無逮譚者。

translations.literal: At that time none of the nine provinces' cultivated and filial examination answers matched Tan.
translations.idiomatic: None in the nine provinces out-argued Tan.

sentences.zh: 譚素以才學為東土所推。

translations.literal: Tan always by talent and learning was esteemed by the eastern lands.
translations.idiomatic: The east already prized Tan's scholarship.

sentences.zh: 同郡劉頌時為廷尉，見之歎息曰：「不悟鄉里乃有如此才也！

translations.literal: Liu Song of the same commandery was then Commandant of Justice—seeing him sighed: "I did not realize my village held such talent!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song, chief justice of his county, sighed, "Who knew our town held such a mind?

sentences.zh: 」博士王濟于眾中嘲之曰：「五府初開，群公辟命，采英奇於仄陋，拔賢俊於岩穴。

translations.literal: " Erudite Wang Ji mocked him before the crowd: "The five offices newly opened—lords summon commands—gather marvels from humble lanes—pull worthies from cliff caves.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji sneered before guests: "High office hunts talent in hovels and caves.

sentences.zh: 君吳、楚之人，亡國之余，有何秀異而應斯舉？

translations.literal: You are a Wu-Chu man—a survivor of a fallen state—what excellence responds to this summons?
translations.idiomatic: You—Wu-Chu remnant—what pearl earns this pick?

sentences.zh: 」譚答曰：「秀異固產于方外，不出於中域也。

translations.literal: " Tan answered: "Excellence indeed is produced beyond the regions—not emerging from the central plain.
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied: "Brilliance grows on the margins—not only in the heartland.

sentences.zh: 是以明珠文貝，生於江、鬱之濱；

translations.literal: Hence bright pearls and patterned shells—are born on Jiang and Yu's shores;
translations.idiomatic: Pearls and cowries shine by Yangzi bays;

sentences.zh: 夜光之璞，出乎荊、藍之下。

translations.literal: night-shining unwrought jade—comes out below Jing and Lan.
translations.idiomatic: night-glow jade rises from Jing and indigo mines.

sentences.zh: 故以人求之，文王生於東夷，大禹生於西羌。

translations.literal: Hence by men seeking them—King Wen was born among eastern Yi—Great Yu born among western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Seek men widely—King Wen rose among eastern tribes; Yu among western Qiang.

sentences.zh: 子弗聞乎？

translations.literal: Have you not heard?
translations.idiomatic: Have you heard?

sentences.zh: 昔武王克商，遷殷頑民於洛邑，諸君得非其苗裔乎？

translations.literal: Of old King Wu conquered Shang—transferred Yin stubborn people to Luoyi—you gentlemen could they not be their descendants?
translations.idiomatic: When Wu conquered Shang he moved Yin loyalists to Luoyi—might you stem from them?

sentences.zh: 」濟又曰：「夫危而不持，顛而不扶，至於君臣失位，國亡無主，凡在冠帶，將何所取哉！

translations.literal: " Ji again said: "When danger comes yet none uphold—when overturn comes yet none prop—reaching to lord and minister losing position—state perishing without lord—all within cap and sashes—what can they take?
translations.idiomatic: Ji pressed: "When the peril goes unmet—throne falls—what good were belted ministers?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「籲！

translations.literal: " He answered: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Tan answered: "Ah!

sentences.zh: 存亡有運，興衰有期，天之所廢，人不能支。

translations.literal: Survival and perdition have their fortune—rise and fall their period—what Heaven casts off—men cannot sustain.
translations.idiomatic: Rise and ruin ride fate—what Heaven ends no hand upholds.

sentences.zh: 徐偃修仁義而失國，仲尼逐魯而逼齊，段幹偃息而成名，諒否泰有時，曷人力之所能哉！

translations.literal: Xu Yan practiced benevolence and righteousness yet lost the state—Confucius fled Lu and was pressed toward Qi—Duan Ganmu rested at home yet achieved fame—indeed obstructed and smooth have their times—how can human force manage!
translations.idiomatic: Kind Xu lost his realm; Confucius fled Lu; Duan Ganmu won fame from seclusion—fortune turns—what can effort do?

sentences.zh: 」濟甚禮之。

translations.literal: " Ji greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji treated him with deep respect.

sentences.zh: 尋除郎中，遷太子舍人、本國中正。

translations.literal: Shortly appointed Gentleman of the Palace—promoted to Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and provincial impartial judge for his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon made Gentleman of the Palace, then attendant to the heir and provincial evaluator.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為鄄城令，過濮水，作《莊子贊》以示功曹。

translations.literal: When mourning ended—he became magistrate of Juancheng—crossing the Pu River—composed "In Praise of Zhuangzi" to show his merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he governed Juancheng—crossing the Pu he wrote "In Praise of Zhuangzi" for his clerk.

sentences.zh: 而廷掾張延為作答教，其文甚美。

translations.literal: But clerk Zhang Yan of the commandery composed a reply instruction—the text very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Zhang Yan answered his essay in splendid prose.

sentences.zh: 譚異而薦之，遂見升擢。

translations.literal: Tan marveling recommended him—thereupon saw promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Tan admired it and recommended Zhang—who rose in rank.

sentences.zh: 及譚為廬江，延已為淮陵太守。

translations.literal: When Tan became prefect of Lujiang—Zhang Yan had already become prefect of Huailing.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan ruled Lujiang, Zhang Yan already governed Huailing.

sentences.zh: 又舉寒族周訪為孝廉，訪果立功名，時以譚為知人。

translations.literal: He also nominated cold-clan Zhou Fang as Filial and Incorrupt—Fang indeed established merit and fame—the age deemed Tan knew men.
translations.idiomatic: He nominated Zhou Fang from a humble clan—Fang earned glory—men praised Tan's eye.

sentences.zh: 以父墓毀去官。

translations.literal: Because father's tomb damaged—left office.
translations.idiomatic: His father's tomb collapsed—he quit office.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書郎。

translations.literal: Shortly appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon named Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永甯初，出為郟令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongning—went out as magistrate of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongning he became magistrate of Jia.

sentences.zh: 于時兵亂之後，境內饑饉，譚傾心撫䘏。

translations.literal: At that time after military chaos—within the borders famine—Tan poured heart into comforting relief.
translations.idiomatic: After war famine stalked his district—Tan poured himself into relief.

sentences.zh: 司徒王戎聞而善之，出穀三百斛以助之。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Rong hearing praised him—issued grain three hundred hu to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong heard and sent three hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 譚甚有政績，再遷廬江內史，加綏遠將軍。

translations.literal: Tan had very good administrative merit—promoted again to Interior Governor of Lujiang—added General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: His rule excelled—he rose to interior governor of Lujiang with the Pacify-the-Distant generalship.

sentences.zh: 時石冰之党陸圭等屯據諸縣，譚遣司馬褚敦討平之。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Bing's faction Lu Gui and others garrisoned and held various counties—Tan dispatched Marshal Chu Dun to punish and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Gui's band held counties for Shi Bing, Tan sent Chu Dun to crush them.

sentences.zh: 又遣別軍擊冰都督孟徐，獲其驍率。

translations.literal: He also dispatched separate troops to strike Bing's commander-in-chief Meng Xu—captured his fierce leader.
translations.idiomatic: Another column struck Meng Xu—taking his fiercest captain.

sentences.zh: 以功封都亭侯，食邑千戶，賜絹千匹。

translations.literal: By merit ennobled Village Marquis—food estate thousand households—silk thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he became Village Marquis—thousand-house fief and thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 陳敏之亂，吳士多為其所逼。

translations.literal: During Chen Min's rebellion—Wu scholars many were forced by him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Min rebelled many Wu scholars served under duress.

sentences.zh: 顧榮先受敏官，而潛謀圖之。

translations.literal: Gu Rong first received office from Min yet secretly plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong took Chen Min's post but secretly schemed against him.

sentences.zh: 譚不悟榮旨，露檄遠近，極言其非，由此為榮所怨。

translations.literal: Tan did not grasp Rong's intent—published a proclamation far and near—stating to the utmost his wrongs—thereby was resented by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Tan missed Rong's plan—sent a harsh proclamation—earning Rong's hate.

sentences.zh: 又在郡政嚴，而與上司多忤。

translations.literal: Also in the commandery his government was strict—yet with superiors many clashed.
translations.idiomatic: He governed strictly and clashed with superiors.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史劉陶素與譚不善，因法收譚，下壽陽獄。

translations.literal: Inspector Liu Tao of Yang Province by nature with Tan not on good terms—thereby by law seized Tan—cast into Shouyang prison.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao, who disliked Tan, jailed him at Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 鎮東將軍周馥與譚素相親善，理而出之。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the East Zhou Fu by nature with Tan mutually intimate and kind—reasoned and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu, eastern commander and Tan's friend, freed him.

sentences.zh: 及甘卓討馥，百姓奔散，馥謂譚已去，遣人視之，而更移近馥。

translations.literal: When Gan Zhuo attacked Fu—common people scattered and fled—Fu thought Tan had gone—sent men to look—yet Tan had moved nearer Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan Zhuo struck Zhou Fu and folk fled, Fu thought Tan gone—but Tan moved closer.

sentences.zh: 馥歎曰：「吾嘗謂華令思是臧子源之疇，今果效矣。

translations.literal: Fu sighed: "I once said Hua Ling Si was of Zang Ziyuan's class—now indeed he proves it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu sighed: "I likened Tan to Zang Hong—he proves it now.

sentences.zh: 」甘卓嘗為東海王越所捕，下令敢有匿者誅之，卓投譚而免。

translations.literal: " Gan Zhuo once was seized by Prince Donghai Si Ma Yue—issued order that whoever harbored him would be executed—Zhuo threw himself on Tan and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo, once hunted by Sima Yue, hid with Tan and lived.

sentences.zh: 及此役也，卓遣人求之曰：「華侯安在？

translations.literal: When this campaign occurred—Zhuo sent men seeking him saying: "Where is Marquis Hua?
translations.idiomatic: In that war Zhuo's men asked, "Where is Marquis Hua?

sentences.zh: 吾甘揚威使也。

translations.literal: I am Gan Yangwei's emissary.
translations.idiomatic: We come from Gan Zhuo's staff.

sentences.zh: 」譚答不知，遺絹二匹以遣之。

translations.literal: " Tan answered not knowing—sent two bolts of silk to dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan feigned ignorance and gave two bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 使反，告卓。

translations.literal: The messenger returned—told Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger reported back.

sentences.zh: 卓曰：「此華侯也。

translations.literal: Zhuo said: "That is Marquis Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo said, "That was Marquis Hua.

sentences.zh: 」復求之，譚已亡矣。

translations.literal: " Seeking again—Tan had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: They searched again—Tan had fled.

sentences.zh: 後為紀瞻所薦，而為顧榮所止遏，遂數年不得調。

translations.literal: Later recommended by Ji Zhan—yet blocked by Gu Rong—thereupon several years obtained no reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan recommended him but Gu Rong blocked—years passed without a post.

sentences.zh: 建興初，元帝命為鎮東軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianxing—Prince Yuan of the east appointed him Libationer Consultant for the army defending the east.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianxing Yuan appointed him army libationer-consultant.

sentences.zh: 譚博學多通，在府無事，乃著書三十卷，名曰《辨道》，上箋進之，帝親自覽焉。

translations.literal: Tan was broadly learned and vastly informed—in the bureau nothing to do—thereupon composed thirty fascicles titled "Discerning the Way"—presented memorial advancing it—the emperor personally reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: Idle at headquarters he wrote thirty chapters, Discerning the Way, which the prince read.

sentences.zh: 轉丞相軍諮祭酒，領郡大中正。

translations.literal: Transferred to Chancellor's army Libationer Consultant—acting provincial senior impartial judge.
translations.idiomatic: He became the chancellor's libationer-consultant and acting chief evaluator.

sentences.zh: 譚薦干寶、范珧於朝，乃上箋求退曰：「譚聞霸主遠聽，以求才為務；

translations.literal: Tan recommended Gan Bao and Fan Yao to court—thereupon presented memorial seeking retirement saying: "Tan has heard the hegemon listens far—takes seeking talent as task;
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Gan Bao and Fan Yao, then asked to retire: "Rulers listen for talent.

sentences.zh: 僚屬量身，以審己為分。

translations.literal: subordinates measure body—take examining self as duty.
translations.idiomatic: Staff must know their limits.

sentences.zh: 故疏廣告老，漢宣不違其志；

translations.literal: Hence Shu Guang announced old age—Han Xuandi did not oppose his intent;
translations.idiomatic: Shu Guang retired—Xuandi let him;

sentences.zh: 幹木偃息，文侯就式其廬。

translations.literal: Duan Ganmu rested at home—Marquis Wen of Wei lowered carriage railing before his hut.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ganmu stayed home—Marquis Wen bowed from his cart.

sentences.zh: 譚無古人之賢，竊有懷遠之慕。

translations.literal: Tan lacks the worthies of antiquity—yet privately harbors longing for distant withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: I lack ancient virtue yet long to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 自登清顯，出入二載，執筆無贊事之功，拾遺無補闕之績；

translations.literal: Since ascending clear prominence—entering and exiting two years—holding brush achieved no praise-worthy tasks—picking omissions none mending gaps merit;
translations.idiomatic: Two years in high office—no deeds worth praise;

sentences.zh: 過在納言，暗於舉善；

translations.literal: fault lies in accepting counsel—dark on recommending good;
translations.idiomatic: I accepted speech yet failed to lift good men;

sentences.zh: 狂寇未賓，復乏謀策。

translations.literal: mad bandits not yet guest—again lacking stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: rebels remain unsubdued—I offered no plans.

sentences.zh: 年向七十，志力日衰，素餐無勞，實宜辭退。

translations.literal: Age nearing seventy—mind and strength daily failing—eating free meals without labor—truly fitting to resign retire.
translations.idiomatic: Near seventy, fading—I eat unearned rice—should retire.

sentences.zh: 謹奉還所假左丞相軍諮祭酒版。

translations.literal: Respectfully return the borrowed tablet of Left Chancellor army Libationer Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: I return the Libationer Consultant seal.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " Not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 建武初，授秘書監，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu—appointed Director of the Palace Library—firmly declined not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu named him palace librarian—he declined.

sentences.zh: 太興初，拜前軍，以疾復轉秘書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing—appointed Forward General—because of illness transferred again to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Taixing made him Forward General—illness moved him back to librarian.

sentences.zh: 自負宿名，恆怏怏不得志。

translations.literal: He bore himself on old reputation—always discontented without achieving his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of old fame he stayed restless.

sentences.zh: 時晉陵硃鳳、吳郡吳震並學行清修，老而未調，譚皆薦為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Feng of Jinling and Wu Zhen of Wu commandery both learning and conduct pure cultivated—old yet unreassigned—Tan all recommended as Assistant Editorial Directors.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended aged scholars Zhu Feng and Wu Zhen as assistant editors.

sentences.zh: 或問譚曰：「諺言人之相去，如九牛毛，寧有此理乎？

translations.literal: Someone asked Tan saying: "The proverb says men apart from one another are like nine ox hairs—can there be this principle?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked whether men truly differ like nine ox hairs.

sentences.zh: 」譚對曰：「昔許由、巢父讓天子之貴，市道小人爭半錢之利，此之相去，何啻九牛毛也！

translations.literal: " Tan answered: "Of old Xu You and Chao Fu yielded the Son of Heaven's nobility—market-lane petty men wrangled over half-coin profit—this distance apart—how only nine ox hairs!
translations.idiomatic: Tan said Xu You and Chao Fu scorned the throne while peddlers fight over cash—that gap exceeds nine ox hairs.

sentences.zh: 」聞者稱善。

translations.literal: " Hearers praised good.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners approved.

sentences.zh: 戴若思弟邈，則譚女婿也。

translations.literal: Dai Ruosi's younger brother Miao was Tan's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yuan's brother Dai Miao married Tan's daughter.

sentences.zh: 譚平生時常抑若思而進邈，若思每銜之。

translations.literal: Tan through life often suppressed Ruosi and advanced Miao—Ruosi always harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Tan favored Miao over Dai Yuan—Yuan nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 殆用事，恆毀譚於帝，由是官塗不至。

translations.literal: When he came to authority—constantly slandered Tan to the emperor—thereby Tan's official path did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan held sway he maligned Tan to the throne—Tan rose no higher.

sentences.zh: 譚每懷觖望，嘗從容言於帝曰：「臣已老矣，將待死秘閣。

translations.literal: Tan always harbored disappointment—once calmly said to the emperor: "Your servant is already old—will await death in the secret pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Tan told the emperor calmly, "I am old—I shall die a minor clerk in the archives.

sentences.zh: 汲黯之言，復存於今。

translations.literal: Ji An's words—again exist today.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An's complaint lives again in me.

sentences.zh: 」帝不懌。

translations.literal: " The emperor was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense.

sentences.zh: 久之，加散騎常侍，屢以疾辭。

translations.literal: After long—added Regular Attendant—Cadet—repeatedly declined citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later he gained cadet attendant rank but often pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 及王敦作逆，譚疾甚，不能入省，坐免。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled—Tan was gravely ill—could not enter the palace—by seat dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled Tan was too sick for court—stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: Died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫，金章紫綬，加散騎常侍，諡曰胡。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Minister of the Brilliant Privy—gold seal purple ribbons—added Regular Attendant—Cadet—posthumous name Hu.
translations.idiomatic: They honored him as Brilliant Household Minister with gold seal and purple ribbon, cadet attendant post, and the posthumous name Hu.

sentences.zh: 二子：化、茂。

translations.literal: Two sons: Hua and Mao.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons, Hua and Mao.

sentences.zh: 化字長風，為征虜司馬，討汲桑，戰沒。

translations.literal: Hua style Changfeng—was Marshal Who Conquers Barbarians—campaigning against Ji Sang—fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Changfeng served as conquer-barbarians marshal against Ji Sang and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 茂嗣爵。

translations.literal: Mao inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mao inherited the title.

translations.literal: Equals sign standing alone in the transmitted text.
translations.idiomatic: The chapter inserts a lone equals sign between sections.

sentences.zh: 袁甫

translations.literal: Yuan Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fu.

sentences.zh: =淮南袁甫，字公胄，亦好學，與譚齊名，以詞辯稱。

translations.literal: = Yuan Fu of Huainan, style Gongzhou—also loved learning—equally famed with Tan—praised for rhetorical debate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Fu of Huainan, courtesy Gongzhou, rivaled Tan in scholarship and debate.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣中領軍何勖，自言能為劇縣。

translations.literal: Once visited Central Protector-General He Xu—himself saying able to govern a demanding county.
translations.idiomatic: He called on He Xu claiming he could run a difficult county.

sentences.zh: 勖曰：「唯欲宰縣，不為台閣職，何也？

translations.literal: Xu said: "You only wish to be county magistrate—not take terrace pavilion office—why?
translations.idiomatic: He Xu asked why he wanted only a county post, not central office.

sentences.zh: 」甫曰：「人各有能有不能。

translations.literal: " Fu said: "Men each have what they can and cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied that each man has strengths and limits.

sentences.zh: 譬繒中之好莫過錦，錦不可以為㡊；

translations.literal: Compare the finest in silk brocade none surpasses brocade—brocade cannot make a hunting canopy;
translations.idiomatic: Brocade tops silk yet cannot sew a hunter's hood;

sentences.zh: 谷中之美莫過稻，稻不可以為贇。

translations.literal: the finest in grain none surpasses rice—rice cannot become vinegar.
translations.idiomatic: rice crowns grain yet cannot brew vinegar.

sentences.zh: 是以聖王使人，必先以器，苟非周材，何能悉長！

translations.literal: Hence sage kings when employing men—must first match vessel—if not all-around timber—how can all grow long!
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings match tools to tasks—no one excels at everything.

sentences.zh: 黃霸馳名於州郡，而息譽於京邑。

translations.literal: Huang Ba made famous name in prefectures and commanderies—yet rested fame in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ba shone in the provinces yet faded at court.

sentences.zh: 廷尉之材，不為三公，自昔然也。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice talent—not becoming Three Dukes—from antiquity thus.
translations.idiomatic: Commandants seldom leap straight to the Three Dukes—always so.

sentences.zh: 」勖善之，除松滋令。

translations.literal: " Xu praised him—appointed magistrate of Songzi.
translations.idiomatic: He Xu agreed and named him magistrate of Songzi.

sentences.zh: 轉淮南國大農、郎中令。

translations.literal: Transferred to Huainan kingdom Grand Minister of Agriculture—Household Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to granary minister and household superintendent of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 石珩問甫曰：「卿名能辯，豈知壽陽已西何以恆旱？

translations.literal: Shi Heng asked Fu saying: "Your fame as debater—do you know why west of Shouyang is always dry?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng asked why lands west of Shouyang stay dry.

sentences.zh: 壽陽已東何以恆水？

translations.literal: East of Shouyang why always flood?
translations.idiomatic: Why east of Shouyang stays soaked?

sentences.zh: 」甫曰：「壽陽已東皆是吳人，夫亡國之音哀以思，鼎足強邦，一朝失職，憤歎甚積，積憂成陰，陰積成雨，雨久成水，故其域恆澇也。

translations.literal: " Fu said: "East of Shouyang are all Wu people—music of a fallen state is mournful and longing—tripod-standing strong state—one morning lost office—resentful sighing greatly accumulates—accumulated worry becomes yin—yin accumulates becomes rain—rain long becomes water—hence that territory always floods.
translations.idiomatic: East of Shouyang was Wu—fallen state's lament bred dark vapors that condensed into endless rain.

sentences.zh: 壽陽已西皆是中國，新平強吳，美寶皆入，志盈心滿，用長歡娛。

translations.literal: West of Shouyang are all Central Lands—newly pacified strong Wu—beautiful treasures all entered—will full heart satisfied—using prolonged joy.
translations.idiomatic: West lies the heartland—fresh from Wu's treasures—bellies full and hearts glad.

sentences.zh: 《公羊》有言，魯僖甚悅，故致旱京師。

translations.literal: The Gongyang says—Duke Xi of Lu greatly pleased—hence brought drought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Gongyang notes Duke Xi's excess joy brought drought on the capital.

sentences.zh: 若能抑強扶弱，先疏後親，則天下和平，災害不生矣。

translations.literal: If able to humble the strong and raise the weak—first distant later kin—then all under Heaven peaceful—disasters do not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Balance strong and weak, kin last—then peace holds and omens cease.

sentences.zh: 」觀者歎其敏捷。

translations.literal: " Observers sighed at his quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners marveled at his wit.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘，卒於家。

translations.literal: Age over eighty—died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died past eighty at home.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians' appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Historians' appraisal.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫緝政厘俗，拔群才以成務；

translations.literal: The historians say: Ordering government and correcting customs—drawing flock talent to accomplish tasks;
translations.idiomatic: Historians say rule and custom turn on gathering talent.

sentences.zh: 振景觀光，俟明主而宣績。

translations.literal: raising brilliance viewing glory—awaiting enlightened lord to proclaim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Merit shines when an enlightened ruler appears.

sentences.zh: 武皇之世，天下乂安，朝廷屬意於求賢，軸有懷於幹祿。

translations.literal: In Martial Emperor's age—all under Heaven peaceful—the court fixed mind on seeking worthies—linchpin bore intent on striving for salary.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu the realm rested—court chased talent while ministers chased posts.

sentences.zh: 郤詵等並韞價州裏，裒然應召，對揚天問，高步雲衢，求之前哲，亦足稱矣。

translations.literal: Xi Shen and others together treasured worth in prefectures and commanderies—solemnly answered summons—responded and raised Heaven's questions—high-stepped cloud avenues—seeking among former wise—also sufficient to be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shen and peers hid talent locally then answered the throne—among past worthies they deserve mention.

sentences.zh: 令思行己徇義，志篤周、甘，仁者必通，抑斯之謂！

translations.literal: Ling Si conducting himself followed righteousness—will earnest toward Zhou and Gan—benevolent men must penetrate—perhaps this speaks!
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tan lived by duty like Zhou Fu and Gan Zhuo—kind men reach far—so goes the verdict.

sentences.zh: 雖才行夙章，而待終秘閣，積薪之恨，豈獨古人乎！

translations.literal: Though talent and conduct early manifest—yet awaiting end in secret pavilion—stacked firewood's regret—how only ancients!
translations.idiomatic: Though gifted he ended a librarian—the piled-faggots regret is not theirs alone.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：郤、阮洽聞，含章體政。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Xi and Ruan broad learning—embracing pattern embodying government.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Xi and Ruan mastered learning and embodied policy.

sentences.zh: 華生毓德，褫巾應命。

translations.literal: Master Hua nurturing virtue—discarding headcloth answering summons.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tan bred virtue and answered the call from reclusion.

sentences.zh: 鳥路曾飛，龍津派泳。

translations.literal: Bird road once flew—dragon ford dispatched swimming.
translations.idiomatic: They flew the bird path and swam the dragon ford.

sentences.zh: 素業可久，高芬斯盛。

translations.literal: Plain enterprise can long endure—high fragrance thus flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Their plain virtue lasts—their fragrance still rises.
